U.S. Treasury Yield Curves, 2019-2024

Source: R/data.R
treasury_yields.Rd

Daily U.S. Treasury constant maturity yields across eleven maturities, in the shape the rest of the package expects: a Date column followed by one column per maturity, named by maturity in years.

Bundled so that the examples, vignettes and tests have a real yield panel to work on without a FRED API key.

Usage

treasury_yields

Format

A data frame with 1,501 rows and 12 columns:

Date

Observation date, ascending.

0.0833, 0.25, 0.5

1-month, 3-month and 6-month yields.

1, 2, 3, 5, 7, 10, 20, 30

1- to 30-year yields.

Yields are in decimal form, so 0.0425 is 4.25 percent. There are no missing values: market holidays, which FRED reports as rows with no observation at any maturity, are excluded rather than carried as NA.

Source

Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED), series DGS1MO, DGS3MO, DGS6MO, DGS1, DGS2, DGS3, DGS5, DGS7, DGS10, DGS20 and DGS30. These are the Treasury constant maturity series of the Federal Reserve's H.15 release, retrieved 2026-10-08 and covering 2 January 2019 to 31 December 2024. As U.S. government works they are in the public domain.

The script that builds this dataset is data-raw/treasury_yields.R in the package sources; it calls get_treasury_yield_data.

Details

Six years of daily observations spans 72 month-ends, which is enough for estimate_dns_dynamics to run in its default monthly sampling mode. The window covers the 2020 collapse to near-zero short rates, the 2022-2023 inversion, and the start of the subsequent normalisation, so it contains level, slope and curvature variation rather than a single regime.

Examples

data(treasury_yields)

# The most recent curve
tail(treasury_yields, 1)
#>            Date 0.0833   0.25    0.5      1      2      3      5      7     10
#> 1501 2024-12-31  0.044 0.0437 0.0424 0.0416 0.0425 0.0427 0.0438 0.0448 0.0458
#>          20     30
#> 1501 0.0486 0.0478

# Dates on which the 3-month yield exceeded the 10-year
inverted <- treasury_yields$`0.25` > treasury_yields$`10`
range(treasury_yields$Date[inverted])
#> [1] "2019-03-22" "2024-12-12"
